interactions.note: You get one Reaction per round. An Opportunity Attack taken before the trigger leaves nothing for the readied response, and a readied response that fires leaves nothing for a later Opportunity Attack. Both directions are tested.
Ready is the turn's action. You can't ready after attacking, and once you have readied you can't take another action such as Attack or Dash.
Trigger timing during movement: the Reaction comes right after the triggering step, in the middle of the move (ambiguity 3).

Holding a spell takes Concentration, so readying one ends an earlier Concentration (ambiguity 1). Readying a weapon attack takes no Concentration. Damage calls for a save, and a failed save makes the held spell dissipate (#9).
The slot is spent when you ready the spell. It isn't refunded if the trigger is ignored, never comes, or Concentration breaks, and releasing the spell spends no second slot.

interactions.with: one spell with a slot per turn
interactions.note: A readied slot spell counts toward the readying turn's one slot spell. Releasing it shouldn't count again. Not tested yet.
The tests name targets when readying and never check range at release, so they hold under either reading.
Bonus Action and Reaction spells are refused, and an action cantrip is allowed.
Readied movement is capped at your Speed. Two questions are untested: does a Speed-0 condition gained after readying stop the move, and does readied movement count against next turn's movement?
Whether an invisible creature's movement counts as 'perceivable' is untested. The register has no ruling on it.

abuse.case: Two Reactions in one round (an Opportunity Attack, then the readied attack)
abuse.reason: There is one Reaction per round.

abuse.case: Two Reactions in one round (the readied attack, then an Opportunity Attack)
abuse.reason: Once the readied attack has fired, the Reaction is spent.
You take the Ready action on your turn.

abuse.case: Two actions in one turn (Attack, then Ready)
Readying an action plus a move as one response
abuse.reason: The response is either the action or a move, not both.

abuse.case: A readied move farther than your Speed
abuse.reason: Readied movement is up to your Speed.

abuse.case: A trigger that names a creature that doesn't exist
abuse.reason: The trigger must be a perceivable circumstance.

abuse.case: Readying a spell with no slot left
abuse.reason: A readied spell is cast as normal and spends its resources.

abuse.case: Getting the slot back when the spell is never released
abuse.reason: The resources are spent when the spell is readied.

abuse.case: Concentration on two spells at once (Bless plus a held spell)

abuse.reason: A readied spell must have a casting time of an action.

abuse.case: A refused command that still spends the turn or a slot
abuse.reason: assert_refused_cleanly checks that nothing changed, and the test also checks the slot count.

rulings_proposed.ambiguity: GLOSS.ready ambiguity 1: 'holding on to the spell’s magic requires Concentration'. Does holding a spell that isn't a Concentration spell end an existing Concentration?
rulings_proposed.ruling: Reading A. Holding any readied spell is an effect that requires Concentration, so readying one ends Concentration on an earlier spell such as Bless.

rulings_proposed.ambiguity: GLOSS.ready ambiguity 2: does an ignored trigger use up the readied action?
rulings_proposed.ruling: Reading A. Ignoring the trigger keeps the readied action and the Reaction for a later occurrence of the same circumstance, until the start of your next turn.

rulings_proposed.ambiguity: GLOSS.ready ambiguity 3: 'right after the trigger finishes'. For a movement trigger, does the Reaction come after the triggering step or after the whole move?
rulings_proposed.ruling: Reading A. The Reaction resolves right after the triggering step and interrupts the rest of the move. The mover then finishes its movement.

rulings_proposed.ambiguity: GLOSS.ready gap: what happens to a held spell that isn't released before the start of your next turn?
rulings_proposed.ruling: The Concentration that holds it ends at the start of your next turn. The spell dissipates without effect, and the spent slot isn't refunded.

rulings_proposed.ambiguity: GLOSS.ready #4: is the readied response checked when you ready it, or only when the trigger occurs?
rulings_proposed.ruling: It is checked when you ready it. A response that isn't one action, or one move up to your Speed, is refused cleanly on your turn before the action is spent.

summary:
The engine has no Ready action: no `ready` command, no structured trigger and no readied Reaction. This attempt adds the four tests the last check found missing:
- **#2 negative:** after Ready, Dash is refused because the action is spent.
- **#3 positive:** only the chosen circumstance triggers the Reaction. Goblin 2 stepping in fires it; the other goblin stepping in doesn't.
- **#6 negative:** an ignored trigger releases nothing, and the slot stays spent.
- **#8 negative:** readying a weapon attack takes no Concentration, so Bless stays up.

That makes 33 GLOSS.ready tests in tests/srd/test_glossary.py, all claimed red and marked xfail(strict) with one shared ticket. Every clause from #1 to #9 has a positive and a negative test. There are boundary tests for #2, #4 and #8, and 12 abuse tests.

Test results:
- The normal run of the file gives 34 passed and 33 xfailed.
- With --runxfail, each of the 4 new tests fails only because Ready is missing: "Unknown command 'ready'", or the step that readies.
- ruff format and ruff check are clean.

The command shape the tests use lives in tests/support/ready.py, so if the dev loop picks a different shape, only that file changes. The new cheats are in loop/abuse-catalogue.md. Five rulings are proposed. There are no scenario changes, since stage B had no verdicts.
